<a id="summary"></a>

## Summary

Delivers req-07 and the request half of req-08 (the notify half is s06). Rulings: C1 (the directory is the authority for role: addressing; if it disagrees with seat_roles the send refuses with a named mismatch), C2 (an --fyi send to a role with no holder still queues and wakes the PA, else the prime), C3 (the role-send receipt prints the request id, which s06's `pij output --answers` uses), C4 (`--reply wake` to a cold requester is an audited forced wake, as the PA watchdog does), C6 (s04's after-assign hook drains the role queue to the new holder).

<a id="goals"></a>

## Goals

- Roadmap 001 s05: `pij send role:<id>[/<instance>]` resolves to exactly one live holder through the directory, queues when there is none and wakes the PA, refuses with a list when there are several, and stores the requester's reply mode.

<a id="non-goals"></a>

## Non-goals

- Anything another roadmap step owns; see roadmap 001.

| ac-0001 | Resolve. `pij send role:&lt;id&gt;` and `role:&lt;id&gt;/&lt;instance&gt;` resolve through the project's directory holders (s04) to exactly one live seat and deliver as a normal send; the receipt prints the request id (C3). A directory/seat_roles disagreement refuses with a named mismatch (C1). | [ ] unchecked | — | — | [bp-0001](assets/backpressure.dd.md#rows) | — |
| ac-0002 | Queue and wake. With no live holder, the request is stored on the role's queue (migration 0034: requests with role, instance, requester, reply mode, limit, state) and the PA (else the prime) is woken once with runnable next steps: revive the last holder (showing its context size) or assign a fresh seat. An --fyi send queues too (C2). The queue appears in the PA's watchdog feed until cleared; no new timer. pij never starts a seat itself. | [ ] unchecked | — | — | [bp-0002](assets/backpressure.dd.md#rows) | — |
| ac-0003 | Drain on assign (C6). Assigning a holder runs the s04 after-assign hook, which delivers that role's queued requests to the new holder in order and marks them delivered. | [ ] unchecked | — | — | [bp-0003](assets/backpressure.dd.md#rows) | — |
| ac-0004 | Several holders. With two or more live holders on the addressed role and instance, the send refuses and lists them. | [ ] unchecked | — | — | [bp-0004](assets/backpressure.dd.md#rows) | — |
| ac-0005 | Reply modes (req-08, request half). `--reply wake\|fyi\|none` (default wake) is stored on the request and returned in the receipt; s06 uses it to notify. `--limit &lt;duration&gt;` is stored for s12 (default: the role's default_limit, C5). | [ ] unchecked | — | — | [bp-0005](assets/backpressure.dd.md#rows) | — |
| ac-0006 | Cost (AGENTS.md, resource cost is a correctness property). Sends to a role cost what a normal send costs; queueing is a store write; the PA wake is one delivery; draining on assign is one delivery per queued request. No new timer or poll; the queue rides the existing watchdog round. | [ ] unchecked | — | — | [bp-0006](assets/backpressure.dd.md#rows) | — |

<a id="execution-guardrails"></a>

## Execution Guardrails

- Tests use scratch repos and a private daemon; never the live governance branch or the prod daemon.
- Builds: your own target or `just shared-build`; CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0; -p scoping; stop under 25 GB free.
- No `git add -A`, no `--no-verify`; no node_modules, never symlinked (C25); TS proof is CI on the exact head.
- Shared seams (crates/cli wiring, skills/pij): rebase onto main before the PR and keep edits minimal; don't fork the seam.
- One push per review round; no pushes after the PR is out for verdicts unless a verdict asks.
